extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists and informed public across disciplines (anthropology, astronomy, plant pathology, instrumentation, and science policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and summarizing scientific news items, book reviews, observational reports, and policy/address content across multiple scientific disciplines for a learned journal readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fothergill trust prize submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors intending to compete should send in a notice of their intention, together with a full description of their inventions, not later than March 31, 1908, to the secretary of the Society of Arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for eligibility for award (gold medal or prize of £20) — a timely notice plus a full description is necessary. (Context: award for portable apparatus/appliance for enabling rescue work in noxious air.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Include music and song texts in ethnographic volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: The second part is intended to include the music und text of the songs referred to, or given only in a free translation, in the present volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer regards inclusion of original music and full song texts as essential material for completeness and future comparative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide comparative study of collected tales
rubrics_metrics.description: It will also comprise a comparative study of the tales and incidents, in which they will be treated in their relation to 'the tales of other tribes of the so-called Caddoan stock,' and, indeed, to those of other American Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative analysis with related groups (and broader indigenous corpora) is considered a 'very necessary complement' to collections of traditional narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give authoritative descriptions of social organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: We want... a fuller description of the social organisation, the rites and beliefs of the stocks than he has hitherto given. We want, for instance, what are the marriage-rules of the tribes, whether descent is traced in the male or the female line, what their clan-organisation is; we want full descriptions of their ceremonies, their taboos, and so forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer stresses need for explicit, authoritative ethnographic statements (marriage rules, descent principles, clan structure, ceremonies, taboos) rather than leaving such matters to inference from stories alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accurate terminology/classification (avoid misleading titles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'mythology' on the title-page is a somewhat unfortunate choice. ... many tales are included which can only be called mythology by an illegitimate extension of the meaning of that word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly works should apply classificatory labels (e.g., 'mythology') carefully and avoid overstretching terms to include tales that are not religious or not believed to be true; accurate labeling aids reader understanding and scholarly utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness in plant pathology treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiment station... has issued... a remarkable publication which not only deals in a very comprehensive and thorough way with the fungus enemies of the sugar-cane, but also contains a series of valuable notes on associated insects and nematodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-quality bulletin should be wide-ranging, covering pathogens and associated organisms (insects, nematodes) that interact with the disease complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed, accurate descriptions and high-quality illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: In this section... we have a most accurate and interesting description of the Ithyphallus fungus... The extraordinary fructifications are detailed and admirably illustrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxonomic/diagnostic accounts should provide precise morphological/biological descriptions and clear, detailed illustrations to support identification and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide experimental evidence and quantitative data
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispersal of this fungus by their agency, especially in the excreta, is proved, and ... the spores are also carried in numbers on the feet. The spores from five of the fly tracks on glass were found to be 860,000 per track. ... the number of spores found in a 'fly-sperm' was shown to be 22,400,000 in some instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good plant-pathology work should include experimental proof of dispersal/mechanisms and quantitative measurements (e.g., spore counts) to substantiate claims about vectors and transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer practical control measures and cultivation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of lime as a fungicide is pointed out, and methods of cultivation given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied research publications should conclude with actionable recommendations (fungicides, cultural practices) so practitioners can implement control strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe under suitable atmospheric/observing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations made... during the period ... were made under nearly perfect atmospheric conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planetary/visual observations (e.g., markings, terminator contours) require excellent seeing conditions; reviewers expect authors to note atmospheric quality when presenting observational claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base dynamical claims on repeated, time-separated observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference in the markings seen near the poles of Venus and alterations in the contour of the terminator suggested a rotation of the planet, a suggestion which was apparently confirmed by the re-appearance of the same aspects after a lapse of nearly twenty-four hours. Two sets of observations... gave the apparent rotation period as 23h. 20m. and 23h. 25m. respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims such as planetary rotation should be supported by repeat observations showing consistent reappearance and independent period estimates; multiple nights and replicated measures strengthen the inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise ephemerides, magnitude estimates, spectrograms and instrument details
rubrics_metrics.description: The daily ephemeris computed by Dr. E. Stromgren for comet 1907d is given up to July 10... An observation at Strassburg on June 17 gave corrections... and the magnitude was estimated as 8.5 or 9.0. ... Spectrograms taken last autumn showed bright lines... measures of some of the sharper ones show a slight 'shift' towards the violet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Astronomical reports should publish computed ephemerides, observed corrections, magnitude estimates, spectrogram analyses (line identifications and shifts), and instrument/plate details to allow verification and follow-up by other observers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific cinematography requires sufficient film speed and orthochromatic properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The fastest films he has been able to obtain have a speed of H. and D. 200, less than half that of ordinary snapshot plates. This speed is quite inadequate for the photography of operations... the chief obstacle ... is lack of films... better suited to the purpose in the matter of speed and orthochromatic properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion-picture work for scientific observation must use films with high sensitivity (speed) and appropriate spectral sensitivity (orthochromatic or panchromatic) to reduce exposure times and capture relevant details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument design should minimize personal equation and exploit improved photographic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: He [Dr. Braun] constructed... a form of transit micrometer that reduced personal equation to a minimum, and of a plan for photographing the sun by monochromatic light, forestalling by many years the work of Hale and Deslandres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement apparatus should be designed to reduce observer bias ('personal equation'); where feasible, photographic/monochromatic techniques that improve precision and reduce subjective error are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and institutional support for basic research beyond immediate practical results
rubrics_metrics.description: The steady, plodding work which culminates in great discoveries is being carried on quite unheeded by the general public... Research as a 'cult' is not understood; the national attitude towards the workers is one of 'payment by results' in the very narrowest sense of the term. There is need... for a minister... The newly formed 'British Science Guild' may... help us in raising the level of public opinion towards the importance of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science policy and public valuation should recognise and support basic, long-term research (not only immediate utilitarian outcomes); institutional mechanisms (ministerial representation, societies) are suggested to raise public understanding and status of research.
